subject: MedLytics post-call: validation matrix & reservation options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@medlytics.ai>, Devon Cho <devon@hyperscale.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedLytics post-call: validation matrix & reservation options

Thanks team — quick recap from this morning's call with Priya (MedLytics) and Devon (Hyperscale rep) plus suggested next steps. High-level takeaways: 

- MedLytics is evaluating dedicated reserved capacity vs hyperscaler TPU/GPU reservations for inference at scale; main concerns are peak concurrency guarantees during batch ingest and graceful degradation (fallback to cloud burst).
- They care about 99th percentile token latency, KV cache hit behavior across sessions, and predictable per-token cost under sustained traffic.
- Procurement wants clear acceptance criteria and an apples-to-apples POC price/commit comparison.

Attached: redwood-medlytics-eval-matrix.xlsx and a sample workload (medlytics-sample-workload.json) that Priya shared.

Proposed next tests (we should align internal scope before sending to Priya):
1) Baseline throughput/latency: run their sample workload across (a) Redwood Dedicated reserved slice (x GPUs, pinned variant), (b) Redwood hosted autoscaled variant, (c) Hyperscaler reserved instances (Devon's config). Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1M tokens.
2) Tail resilience: simulate a 3x sudden spike for 30 minutes to validate fallback behavior and cold-start impact.
3) Cache & warm-start: evaluate prefix cache reuse across typical sessions (they have many similar document prompts).
4) Quantization variant impact: run same tests with int8-int4 quantized model that keeps quality within their eval thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- p99 generation latency <= 450ms for typical prompt mix at target concurrency (see sample workload).
- No more than 10% errors or timeouts during 3x spike window; fallback to hosted model must keep 95% of requests below 1s.
- Sustained cost delta vs hyperscaler reservation <= 20% (unless we can trade for better latency).

Asks for internal owners: Jordan — can you propose a concrete hardware slice (GPU type + count) and estimated price for a 3-month reserved commit? Marissa — can you own scheduling the POC and Ops runbook? Rishi — can you confirm whether we can produce an SLA/ops playbook that includes automatic fallback to hosted nodes?

I'll draft a succinct one-pager to send to Priya once we align.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedLytics post-call: validation matrix & reservation options

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few clarifications and a suggested test matrix we should run in parallel: 

Clarifications needed from MedLytics (I can call Priya if you want):
- Confirm peak concurrency target: their slide said 1.2k concurrent generation users — is that sustained or burst? We need target QPS and average tokens per request.
- Which model family are they comfortable with for the POC? We recommended the 7B-13B class in call, but their procurement asked about a 70B option for quality-sensitivity use cases.

Suggested internal test matrix (quick):
A) Latency sweep: 50/200/500 concurrent generators; measure p50/p95/p99.
B) Reservation sizing: 1/2/4/8 GPU slices — measure utilization and marginal cost per 10k tokens.
C) Failover timing: orchestrate a controlled failover from dedicated -> hosted in under 60s and record tail latency.

For the reserved commit price: my initial slice proposal for the 1.2k target (assuming 13B quantized variant): 4x A800-equivalent GPUs dedicated with 1200 concurrent slots (continuous) — rough monthly commit estimate $72k/mo (we should refine with finance). For hyperscaler, Devon quoted a committed-price equivalent that looked 10-15% cheaper on unit price but without our built-in KV cache and routing that would reduce effective tokens.

I'll run a quick capacity simulation this afternoon and attach estimated utilization curves. If we want to push negotiation, we can propose a graduated commitment: 3-month pilot reserved at 50% commit, with 12-month upsell options.

Jordan
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <priya@medlytics.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medlytics.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedLytics post-call: validation matrix & reservation options

Thanks Karthik and Jordan — helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Peak concurrency: we typically see 1.2k concurrent requests during ingest windows (these are 8am-10am PST and 4pm-5pm PST) for ~20 minutes each, plus a baseline of ~300 concurrent during the day. The 1.2k is a burst.
- Average tokens per request: ~120 tokens. For the quality-critical flows we might need the 70B family but are open to evaluating 13B quantized if the quality delta is acceptable.
- Procurement asks for a true comparison: we need committed pricing and an ops SLA (SLOs + escalation path). Also please include an explicit rollback/fallback playbook in case a reserved pool hits sustained errors.

We can run the sample workload attached earlier. For the POC timeline, procurement wants a short commercial proposal we can share internally by Friday (20 Nov).

Thanks — Priya
Head of Platform
MedLytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@medlytics.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MedLytics post-call: validation matrix & reservation options

Great — thanks for the clarity, Priya. Draft next commercial/technical proposal plan (we'll turn into a one-pager + quick pricing table):

1) Proposal A: 3-week Dedicated Pilot (reserved slice): 4x A800-equivalent GPUs, pinned model variant (13B quantized). Cost: $54k for pilot (includes ops support, 24/7 escalation during pilot). Acceptance criteria: p99 <= 450ms at 300 concurrent sustained; degrade gracefully under 1.2k 20-min spikes with <= 15% requests over 1s.
2) Proposal B: Hyperscaler reserved commit equivalent for same capacity (Devon provided rough numbers). We'll include the raw unit cost from Devon but call out differences: no automatic KV prefix cache, longer cold-start behavior, and routing complexity that may increase effective token count by ~8-12%.
3) Hybrid path: 6-week staged commit — start with Pilot A (50% commit) + hosted fallback, then convert to 6/12-month reserved with explicit SLO credits and quarterly performance reviews.

Operational items I'll attach to the one-pager: acceptance test checklist, runbook for failover, measurement plan, and a proposed DocuSign link for an NDA/POC SOW. Marissa — please draft the runbook and schedule the 3-week window; we will aim to start the week of Nov 29 if procurement signs off by 20 Nov.

I'll also include a short section that quantifies effective token economics: show raw unit price vs. effective price after caching and batching benefits from Redwood. Jordan — please share the utilization simulation you mentioned; Rishi please confirm fallback SLA language we can offer during pilot (we can't promise full enterprise SLA during pilot but can offer time-bound credits).

Karthik
